Eighteen comments

The Knockabout Polka

A no-frills version of this lovely three part polka. James Kelly does a great fiddlistic version of it on The Ring Sessions.

Dear Zina, if you would like this tune to link up with that recording adjust the title on track 8 from “knockaboul” to “knockabout”.

-Will Duty

↳ Posted by Test on May 17th, 2004.

Mistake

Sorry, my mistake. It appears the title was correct as entered on the Ring Sessions (and “Knockabout” is an alternate title).

↳ Posted by Test on May 17th, 2004.

Denis Murphy’s/Knocknabowl

Also known as “Denis Murphy’s”, but I’m not adding that to the list of alternative titles because it’ll probably automatically link to about another 20 recordings. Recorded on the “Outlet” label by “Ar Leithidi”, a group which I think featured most of the Dublin O’Brien family. Shouldn’t it be “Knocknabowl” ?

↳ Posted by Kenny on May 17th, 2004.

Knocknaboul, County Kerry, Sliabh Luachra, Ireland

East of Killarney, between Castleisland and Rathmore, Killarney and Newmarket…

↳ Posted by ceolachan on December 14th, 2014.

Knocknaboul, County Kerry, Sliabh Luachra, Ireland

Ceol -- perhaps we are discussing two different places, but I would think that this was one from the Williamstown-Castleisland road in the townland Knocknaboul, just east of the ambush site in Tureengarrive. Padraig being from Glentann Cross, just a townland over, it would seem likely that it was his, albeit not originally.

The Knocknaboul, X:5

First heard this at the session at The Fiddle & Pick, Pegram, TN, USA, played with enthusiasm. Lots of fun. Recorded it so I could learn it. The double stop/chromatic slides into the next double stop, of course :).

The Knocknaboul #2, X:8

This wonderful 3 part polka, I, imperfectly, learnt from the Star Above The Garter. It is one of my favourite polkas and a great tune to introduce into a set in a session. This setting has been mostly transcribed, from the LP of Denis Murphy and Julia Clifford, by Pat Slattery. The third part, as transcribed, I find beyond my capability, so the second, simplified form is closer to what I aim for.
Pádraig O’Keeffe past this on to many of his pupils but I’ve not heard POK playing it. An example is the setting he gave to Mrs Katie Horan sometime between 1942 and 1949
https://www.itma.ie/digital-library/score/padraig_okeeffe_horan_ms_046
As often, it had no name and it was only a basic version in with the firstv two parts.

↳ Posted by brailsford on April 10th, 2022.

The Knocknaboul, X:9

This setting is played by a flute-and-fiddle-and-harmonica player (also) named David who comes to the Columbus Ohio area sessions fairly regularly - in this case, as part of a set with the Gurteen Cross that he plays with his fiddle in gypsy position and accompanies himself on the harmonica! Amazing! As I recall, he’s been playing instruments since before I was born. I love the turn of phrase in the penultimate measures Ae/g|fd/B/ ca | G2- g - which I didn’t see in any of the present settings.

↳ Posted by skylos on January 16th, 2024.
